name: NullSquare
author: nullsquare

sections.description:
NullSquare connects your WordPress site to the NullSquare external security service. It helps verify control of the site’s domain, keeps the connected-site status synchronized, and can display an optional public trust badge after verification.

The plugin does not scan the WordPress installation, inspect post content, or monitor individual visitors. Security assessments are performed by the separate NullSquare service only for targets the account owner is authorized to test.

Features include:

  • Account-bound domain verification through a signed WordPress REST API challenge.
  • Connected and verified status in Settings > NullSquare.
  • Periodic connection and status synchronization.
  • An optional trust badge that is disabled by default.
  • Footer, floating bottom-right, or manual shortcode placement.
  • Light, dark, and automatic badge themes.
  • Account reconnection and disconnection controls.

A NullSquare account and an internet connection are required to connect and verify a site. Service availability, account eligibility, and any plan limits are governed by NullSquare’s Terms of Service.

External service

This plugin connects to the NullSquare service at api.nullsquare.net and app.nullsquare.net. The service is required for account authorization, domain verification, connection-status synchronization, the public verified-site profile, and badge configuration synchronization.

The plugin does not contact NullSquare until a WordPress administrator explicitly starts a connection. Once connected, it communicates with NullSquare when completing the connection, during scheduled heartbeats, when an administrator visits WordPress admin after the synchronization interval, when settings are saved, and when the administrator disconnects the site.

Depending on the action, the plugin may send:

  • The WordPress site URL, home URL, normalized domain, and verification URL.
  • The WordPress version and NullSquare plugin version.
  • The public site name and the URLs of the WordPress Site Icon or theme logo.
  • Badge enabled state, placement, theme, label, profile URL, and last-rendered timestamp.
  • A short-lived authorization state or connection code.
  • A connected-site identifier and site-specific secret used to authenticate synchronization requests.

The public verification endpoint can return the requested challenge, normalized domain, site URL, a challenge signature, and WordPress/plugin versions. It does not expose the connection code or site-specific secret.

NullSquare may use the public site name, icon, logo, domain, and verification status on the site’s public verified profile after the administrator connects the site. The optional badge links to that public profile only after the administrator enables the badge.

The plugin does not send WordPress posts, pages, comments, user passwords, or individual visitor identities to NullSquare.

  • Service: https://nullsquare.net/
  • Terms of Service: https://nullsquare.net/legal/terms/
  • Privacy Policy: https://nullsquare.net/legal/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Install NullSquare from the WordPress Plugin Directory, or upload the plugin ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Settings > NullSquare.
  4. Review the optional badge setting. It is disabled by default.
  5. Select Connect NullSquare and sign in to your NullSquare account.
  6. Approve the connection and return to WordPress.
  7. Confirm that the plugin reports the site as connected and verified.
  8. Optionally enable the badge, choose its placement and theme, and select Save and Sync.

For manual badge placement, choose Manual shortcode only and insert [nullsquare_badge] in the desired shortcode-compatible area.
sections.faq:
Is a NullSquare account required?

Yes. The plugin is a connector for the external NullSquare service. An account is required to authorize, verify, and synchronize the site.

Does the plugin contact NullSquare immediately after activation?

No. It does not send a request to NullSquare until a WordPress administrator explicitly starts a connection. Periodic synchronization begins only after a successful connection.

Does this plugin scan my WordPress site?

No. The plugin provides account connection, domain verification, synchronization, and the optional badge. Any security assessment is performed separately by the NullSquare service for an authorized target.

Is the public badge enabled automatically?

No. The badge is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled by a WordPress administrator.

How do I place the badge manually?

Choose Manual shortcode only in Settings > NullSquare, then add [nullsquare_badge] to a shortcode-compatible location.

What happens when I disconnect?

The plugin asks NullSquare to revoke the connection, removes the local connection credentials, disables the badge, and stops authenticated synchronization.

What should I do before uninstalling?

Use the Disconnect action first so NullSquare can revoke the remote connection. Uninstalling then removes the plugin’s local settings and scheduled heartbeat.
sections.changelog:
0.2.1

  • Enqueued admin styles with wp_add_inline_style() instead of an inline style tag.
  • Unslashed and sanitized all administrator form input at the point of access.
  • Added translator comments and ordered placeholders for translatable strings.
  • Used wp_safe_redirect() with a scoped allowed-host filter for the authorization redirect.

0.2.0

  • Initial WordPress.org submission.
  • Added account-bound domain verification and connection status.
  • Added periodic synchronization and disconnect support.
  • Added an optional, administrator-controlled trust badge.
